idea.description: Add a bounded recent-anchor transition-lift residual to each dataset’s SASRec. Construct distinct-user directed adjacent-transition counts from training histories, shrink conditional probabilities toward transition-target popularity, and aggregate positive lift over the last five causal anchors. Learn one bounded amplitude per dataset. Exclude each training example’s entire user from every statistic used for its residual; use all training users for validation and inference. Unlike the previous inspiration, this proposal uses fixed count-derived transition scores instead of separate learned source/target embeddings and a feature-conditioned gate. Treat it as an interpretable sequential-rule/SASRec fusion experiment rather than a new model class.
idea.motivation: The residual explicitly targets broad associations outranking recent intent and speculative specialized upgrades lacking behavioral support. Recent directed successors provide a limited behavioral reason to recommend an item now; other-user support is stronger evidence than a target’s own inclusion in its transition table. Neither establishes compatibility, equipment ownership, replacement needs, or purchase completion. Quantitatively, the intervention targets weak positive–negative separation, especially Electronics’ 14.95% wrong-ranking rate and negative lower-tail margin. These diagnostics justify investigation, not a claim of higher validation HR@10. The method does not directly address already satisfied needs and is not eligible to claim that failure is solved.
idea.implementation_notes:
Algorithm specification: For each dataset and training user u, construct the set E_u of nonpadding adjacent directed pairs. Count c(i,j)=sum_u 1[(i,j) in E_u]. Let C(i)=sum_j c(i,j), T(j)=sum_i c(i,j), M=sum_j T(j), and p0(j)=(T(j)+1)/(M+N), over the fixed N real catalog items. C(i) counts distinct-user-edge incidences, not distinct source users. Define p(j|i)=(c(i,j)+20*p0(j))/(C(i)+20). For observed edges, define r(i,j)=C(i)/(C(i)+10) * c(i,j)/(c(i,j)+3) * clip(log(p(j|i)/p0(j)),0,2). Set r=0 for unobserved edges and padding. Initial constants are engineering defaults, not estimated optima. This is a smoothed, positive clipped log-lift statistic. It resembles positive PMI only under a consistent edge-incidence sampling interpretation; it is not an estimate of causal complementarity or occurrence-weighted next-purchase probability.

Required exclusion during training: A training user’s examples must use c_minus_u(i,j)=c(i,j)-1[(i,j) in E_u], C_minus_u(i)=C(i)-outdegree_E_u(i), T_minus_u(j)=T(j)-indegree_E_u(j), and M_minus_u=M-|E_u|. Recompute p0_minus_u(j)=(T_minus_u(j)+1)/(M_minus_u+N), the conditional probability, source reliability, edge reliability and clipped lift from these quantities. Set the result to zero when c_minus_u(i,j)=0. Repeated occurrences of one edge by u contribute one subtraction, not the occurrence count. Keep the catalog and item mapping fixed; exclusion changes statistics, not preprocessing or the benchmark split. Handle users with no edges and M_minus_u=0. Smoothing does not replace user exclusion. This is analogous to leave-one-out target-statistic handling, with the user as the exclusion group, as motivated by H2O leakage handling, scikit-learn cross-fitting, and GroupKFold principles. It prevents direct self-contribution to the statistic, but does not make the entire supervised model independent of that user.

Training-only population counts can use all permitted training histories; per-position anchors must use only the causal prefix through that position. Other training users’ later training events may enter these aggregate statistics. This follows the supplied static split protocol and is not a claim of globally chronological online evaluation. Never use validation or test interactions in counts or exclusion tables. At inference use the full training-only table. The resulting other-user-training/full-training-inference feature shift is intentional and must be disclosed. It is largest for sparse edges; report its sensitivity rather than assuming exclusion eliminates every form of overfitting.

At position t, use up to five nonpadding anchors ending at t, with weights 2^(-age/2), where age is the anchor’s interaction offset, not elapsed clock time. The residual is their weighted mean r, dividing by all nonpadding anchor weights rather than only supported anchors. This prevents a single weakly covered anchor from receiving full weight. Repeated anchors retain their recency-weighted contributions; no semantic labels are inferred. Score s(t,j)=SASRecScore(t,j)+a*residual(t,j), where a=2*sigmoid(theta), initialized to 0.01, hence theta=logit(0.005), approximately -5.2933. The total additive contribution lies in [0,4]. Preserve the baseline optimizer, negative sampler and loss initially; include theta in the optimizer with zero weight decay so regularization does not mechanically push a toward 1. Keep all existing backbone parameter-group settings. Positive-only lift cannot directly penalize unsupported recommendations, so it may fail to displace them when supported alternatives are absent.

Optimization caveat: For BCE-with-logits and an individual example, dL/dtheta=(sigmoid(s+a*r)-y)*r*a*(1-a/2), before any batch weighting or reduction. At a=0.01 the amplitude derivative factor is 0.00995. Correctly saturated predictions attenuate it further; incorrectly saturated predictions need not have small logit gradients. Adam updates are not proportional to raw gradient magnitudes, so gate initialization alone does not establish stalled learning. Log a, its gradient magnitude, residual coverage, and actual changes in candidate orderings. A frozen-checkpoint amplitude sensitivity analysis tests whether the residual has useful ranking information independently of joint amplitude optimization.

Implementation of sparse statistics: Store sorted int64 edge keys i*(N+1)+j and counts, plus source totals, target totals and total incidence mass. Validate int64 key bounds. Use searchsorted with explicit bounds and exact-match checks, including empty tables. For training exclusion, also store sorted user-edge membership keys or per-user sorted edge lists, per-user sparse source/target incidence degrees and |E_u|. Compute excluded quantities on demand without materializing a table for every user. Do not overwrite global counts while processing a batch. For inference precompute the full-training residual values on observed edges and omit user-exclusion structures from the exported predictor if they are unnecessary there. Compute recent-anchor contributions sequentially or in chunks to avoid a B*L*K*5 allocation. Document tensor broadcasts for B x L targets, B x L x K negative candidates, and final-state candidate lists; never mix users or positions. Store the exact item mapping, counts/statistics, architecture configuration and checkpoints beneath the trial directory.

User identity is required for exclusion, but the public diagnostic loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative). Do not infer user identity from a truncated sequence, since different users may share it. The internal training sampler must retain the originating user ID for each sampled sequence and pass that ID explicitly to the training scorer. It may use a private training-batch representation. Supply a separate diagnostic adapter yielding exactly the required four-tuple with None in its first field. This changes neither examples nor splits. The model’s ordinary predict_score uses full-training statistics; its training-only scoring method takes explicit user IDs and computes excluded statistics. No mutable global user context is permitted. Both paths share the same lift and aggregation functions, differing only in their permitted counts.

Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four category routes and int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS', '200')). Use one GPU. Update the predictor writer to emit the identical model class and inference scoring implementation. Keep log2feats(sequence) tensor-valued by concatenating the SASRec state with five anchor-ID channels, stored in float64 to preserve integer IDs; verify runtime ID round trips, and cast the hidden-state slice back to the model dtype before scoring. Construct anchors in integer tensors before conversion and do not pass this packed tensor through autocast or layers that reduce its precision. Float64 packing adds memory and conversion overhead; record it. Alternatively use a structured feature object only if every existing consumer is adapted consistently. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, with loader batches (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B x L. Only public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps are authorized; this first experiment requires histories only. Embedding similarity measures the backbone table and cannot diagnose the count residual itself.

Diagnostic distinction: The unchanged public probe uses full-training inference statistics, so its training-target margins can benefit from their users’ inclusion in the table. Label this limitation explicitly; those margins are descriptive training-fit measurements, not independent-support evidence. Add a separate user-aware training diagnostic through the private sampler to measure excluded-count margins, retaining original metric names and definitions for unchanged outputs and distinct names for added outputs. Compare the same sampled positions and negatives under full versus excluded statistics. Diagnostics with no access to correct user IDs must not claim to compute exclusion.

Assessments, with higher difficulty indicating greater implementation effort:
1. Two-window causal pooling: Originality 3/10 (+ lightweight synthesis of temporal views; - multiscale interests are established). Potential 6/10 (+ can adapt to changing intent; - fixed windows are coarse). User alignment 7/10 (+ emphasizes current and sustained preferences; - supplies no equipment evidence). Model alignment 5/10 (+ may improve confusing states; - no direct evidence it fixes margin tails). Difficulty 3/10 (+ pooling and a gate are small additions; - causal masking and export still need care). Minimal algorithm: causally pool the latest five and all available prefix states, learn a sigmoid mixing gate, and preserve the baseline loss. MIMAR-SRec and the supplied MARS summary motivate temporal scales; their reported results do not establish gains here.
2. Recent-anchor transition lift: Originality 3/10 (+ combines support exclusion, shrinkage and bounded fallback in a precise SASRec experiment; - sequential rules, lift, recency aggregation, target-statistic exclusion and residual fusion are established). Potential 6/10 (+ isolates interpretable independent-population-evidence hypotheses; - sparse coverage and confounding limit breadth). User alignment 6/10 (+ explicitly prioritizes recent supported successors over broad association and unsupported upgrades; - observed successors do not verify practical suitability and positive-only evidence cannot enforce abstention). Model alignment 6/10 (+ directly changes confusing candidate orderings; - can raise false positives and does not improve unsupported edges). Difficulty 5/10 (+ only one additional learned scalar; - exact user exclusion, private sampler IDs, sparse lookup, causal anchors and full-catalog parity materially increase integration work). This revises the earlier originality 4, potential 7, user alignment 7 and difficulty 4 ratings.
3. Multi-negative gBCE: Originality 2/10 (+ a clean objective control; - directly follows published machinery). Potential 7/10 (+ stronger sampled discrimination may transfer across datasets; - gains depend on sampling and compute). User alignment 5/10 (+ better ranking could increase clear matches; - no explicit mechanism for current intent or unsupported equipment). Model alignment 8/10 (+ directly addresses weak sampled separation; - diagnostic negatives need not reflect validation candidates). Difficulty 4/10 (+ published loss is compact; - multiple-negative memory and exclusions require care). Minimal algorithm: retain SASRec, replace the single-negative objective with the published multi-negative gBCE formulation, and preserve the evaluation protocol. This is a separate future trial, not part of the present allocation.

Selection rationale: Retain the transition experiment at 0% progress because it directly addresses two diagnosed user failures and provides a bounded, interpretable test. Its practical-support hypothesis is weaker than a compatibility model, and gBCE has stronger direct alignment with sampled-margin diagnostics. Do not add prototypes, text encoders, hard mining, or a new architecture before testing whether the fixed residual has independent support and useful score magnitude. Three atomic candidate ideas remain sufficient; the additional controls below diagnose the chosen mechanism rather than introduce another model family.

Prespecify three variants: unchanged SASRec, last-anchor count residual, and five-anchor count residual. The last-anchor variant uses only the most recent nonpadding item; all other count definitions, exclusion rules and settings are identical. Allocate at most 12,000 GPU-seconds per variant across all four datasets, split equally; reserve 7,200 seconds for diagnostics, validation overhead, debugging and failures. Count every GPU cost toward 43,200 seconds. The category training cap is 3,000 GPU-seconds or the configured epoch limit, normally 200. Save checkpoints at cumulative training GPU-time milestones of 1,000, 2,000 and 3,000 seconds per category, reusing completed checkpoints when training ends earlier. Pause between complete optimizer updates, save RNG and optimizer state, and record actual milestone overshoot. Avoid starting an update that would exceed the remaining conservative time allowance; otherwise stop and charge any overshoot against the reserve without exceeding the shared total.

Timing boundaries must be explicit: training time includes GPU work for forward passes, sparse training statistics, backward passes and optimizer steps; validation, parity tests, simulator scoring and diagnostic GPU work consume the reserve. Log CPU preprocessing separately, and conservatively charge occupied GPU wall time where phase separation is uncertain. Synchronize CUDA at measurement boundaries. Run compared variants on identical GPU hardware; avoid concurrent work on the same GPU during timing. Record dataset, hardware, total charged GPU-seconds, phase overhead, effective epochs, optimizer updates, examples and valid positions processed, batch size, accumulation and seconds/update at every checkpoint. Equal time need not mean equal optimization. Report HR@10 against charged time and updates using cached evaluations. The host's final held-out inference remains separate. If runtime estimates show the reserve cannot cover the prescribed evaluations, record one budget revision before comparative execution; do not silently omit costs or introduce an adaptive allocation after seeing validation outcomes.

Use the corresponding milestone checkpoint from each of the four datasets as one bundle, giving nine primary variant/milestone combinations, with duplicate completed bundles disclosed. Validate each through the pinned host procedure. Select solely by macro validation HR@10. Exact ties prefer baseline, then last-anchor, then five-anchor, then the earlier milestone within that variant. Disclose all nine scores, per-dataset values where exposed, tie rules, and prior adaptive searches. If simulator runs or diagnostics fail, charge their costs and preserve the failure record. Do not launch the other proposed ideas within this allocation.

Prespecified diagnostic controls: On the final available baseline bundle, disable the residual to reproduce baseline scores exactly, then evaluate fixed amplitudes {0, 0.01, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 2} for the five-anchor table. Cache candidate base scores and residuals and perform arithmetic on CPU when the host exposes the necessary permitted outputs. The diagnostic endpoint 2 is an explicit fixed-amplitude override, not a finite sigmoid parameter. Inspect the score curve without allowing these diagnostic settings to enter primary selection. Any validation-tuned winner from this grid would add selection opportunities and must instead be declared a new budgeted candidate before execution. If pinned evaluation outputs are insufficient, omit the curve and report unavailability; do not reconstruct hidden candidates or alter the evaluator. For jointly trained models, evaluate identical checkpoints with amplitude set to zero to separate the residual's immediate contribution from backbone changes, subject to reserve costs. The matched unchanged-SASRec time/update records are the continued-training control; differences are not automatically causal evidence because backbones followed different gradients. Frozen-backbone BCE-trained amplitude, transition-only scoring, count/confidence versus lift, and cosine item-kNN are useful subsequent controls, explicitly deferred rather than claimed to fit this initial budget. Last-anchor versus five-anchor aggregation is already a primary ablation.

Support diagnostics require no retraining. Compare ordinary edge coverage mean[c(i,j)>0] with user-excluded coverage mean[c_minus_u(i,j)>0] over actual adjacent training-target positions. Ordinary coverage is necessarily 100% for included nonpadding adjacent edges; it is not evidence of generalization. In contrast, score coverage over sampled negatives, validation candidates, or nonadjacent older anchors need not be 100%. Report support buckets 1, 2, 3–5 and >5 distinct users, singleton disappearance rate, and paired changes in smoothed lift after removing the user's numerator, denominator and prior contributions. Report unique-edge summaries, distinct-user-edge summaries and occurrence-weighted summaries separately; optionally report equal-user averages. Macro-average category summaries equally. Define singleton disappearance as the fraction of queried edge incidences whose original support was one and becomes zero, and also report the conditional fraction among singleton-supported incidences, which is identically 100% under exact exclusion. Distinguish disappearance from mere clipping of positive lift to zero. These diagnostics measure independent support and sensitivity, not recommendation accuracy or online temporal validity.

Verify exported versus training-inference candidate scores and candidate versus chunked full-catalog scores, covering all routes, item indexing, padding, truncation, last valid position, ties, candidate broadcasting, seen-item masks, batching, chunk sizes and reloads. Require float32 scorer agreement within atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4, record maximum score errors and ranking disagreements, and resolve top-10 disagreements. The export is compared against the full-training inference path, not the excluded training path. Separately verify exact exclusion against explicit recounting on small training-only examples, including repeated edges, singleton edges, empty support, and removal of source/target totals and prior mass. Track edge coverage, added-score magnitude, amplitude trajectory, original and excluded margin statistics, and source/target popularity strata.

Uncertainty reporting: If the pinned evaluator exposes per-user hit indicators, cache them for all nine primary bundles without changing users, candidates or evaluation seed 42. Bootstrap 200 users with replacement independently within each category, reuse identical resampled indices across models/checkpoints, and average the four category hit-rate differences equally. Use 10,000 CPU-only replicates, analysis RNG seed 42 and percentile 95% intervals. Report category deltas and paired discordant hit counts. One hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. These intervals condition on fixed datasets, training seeds, candidates and trained models. They exclude training-seed and candidate-sampling variability, are not selection-adjusted, and do not establish full-catalog performance. Repeat primary selection inside each bootstrap only as a descriptive stability analysis, reporting selection frequencies and score-gap stability, not unbiased winner performance. Confirmatory claims require a predefined comparison family and an explicitly specified multiplicity-adjusted procedure; no such claim is made here. If per-user hits are unavailable, report aggregate scores and omit bootstrap intervals rather than fabricate them.

Run the required twenty-user full-catalog unseen-item simulator protocol, five real training users per category. Track clear matches, uncertain relevance, unsupported equipment assumptions and broad-association failures using its available feedback. Do not infer unobserved diversity or conformity traits. Simulator feedback and sampled validation are different observations; select only by unchanged host macro validation HR@10. Freeze the winner before the separate held-out evaluation. Counts, learned SASRec representations and validation selection can still exploit popularity, recurring user cohorts, exposure patterns or repeated benchmark opportunities. Lift normalization and user exclusion mitigate specific shortcuts without removing them. The supplied 0.5287 inspiration score is historical context, not evidence for this algorithm.

# Specification for integration into the supplied per-dataset baseline.
# Preserve preprocessing, routing, evaluator, baseline loss and sampler distribution.
# DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; preprocessing seed=0; training seed=42.
# epoch_limit = int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS', '200'))

for dataset in FOUR_DATASETS:
    edges_by_user = {}
    counts = Counter()
    for uid, history in training_histories[dataset].items():
        edges = {(i, j) for i, j in zip(history[:-1], history[1:])
                 if i != 0 and j != 0}
        edges_by_user[uid] = edges
        for edge in edges:
            counts[edge] += 1

    source = sum_counts_by_source(counts)
    target = sum_counts_by_target(counts)
    total = sum(counts.values())
    user_outdegree, user_indegree = sparse_user_edge_degrees(edges_by_user)

    def edge_residual(source_ids, candidates, uid=None):
        # Explicit broadcasting must preserve batch, position and candidate axes.
        c = sparse_edge_lookup(counts, source_ids, candidates, default=0)
        C = lookup(source, source_ids, default=0)
        T = lookup(target, candidates, default=0)
        M = total
        if uid is not None:
            # uid is explicit and correctly broadcast for each training example.
            c = c - user_edge_membership(edges_by_user, uid, source_ids, candidates)
            C = C - lookup(user_outdegree, uid, source_ids, default=0)
            T = T - lookup(user_indegree, uid, candidates, default=0)
            M = M - user_edge_count(edges_by_user, uid)
        p0 = (T + 1.0) / (M + num_real_items)
        conditional = (c + 20.0 * p0) / (C + 20.0)
        lift = clip(log(conditional / p0), 0.0, 2.0)
        value = C / (C + 10.0) * c / (c + 3.0) * lift
        return where((c > 0) & (source_ids != 0) & (candidates != 0), value, 0.0)

    model = BaselineSASRecWithSparseResidual(training_only_statistics)
    model.theta = Parameter(logit(0.01 / 2.0))
    # Add theta to the baseline optimizer with zero weight decay.

    def score(hidden, causal_anchor_ids, candidates, uid=None, fixed_amplitude=None):
        numerator = zeros_like_candidate_scores(hidden, candidates)
        denominator = zeros_like_position_counts(hidden)
        for age in range(num_anchors):  # 1 or 5, fixed by variant
            anchor = causal_anchor_ids[..., age]
            weight = (2.0 ** (-age / 2.0)) * (anchor != 0)
            values = edge_residual(anchor, candidates, uid=uid)
            numerator += broadcast(weight) * values
            denominator += weight
        residual = numerator / broadcast(clamp_min(denominator, 1e-8))
        amplitude = 2.0 * sigmoid(model.theta)
        if fixed_amplitude is not None:
            amplitude = fixed_amplitude  # diagnostic override only
        return baseline_dot_score(hidden, candidates) + amplitude * residual

    for uid, sequence, positive, negative in private_training_sampler:
        # Preserve original sequence sampling, positives and negatives.
        hidden = model.backbone.log2feats(sequence)
        anchors = causal_last_nonpadding_items(sequence, maximum=num_anchors)
        valid = (sequence != 0) & (positive != 0)
        positive_score = score(hidden, anchors, positive, uid=uid)
        negative_score = score(hidden, anchors, negative, uid=uid)
        loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(positive_score, negative_score, valid)
        optimize(loss)
        respect_prespecified_compute_and_checkpoint_schedule()

    # Public diagnostic adapter preserves the required batch contract.
    diagnostic_loader = strip_user_ids_to_none(private_diagnostic_batches)
    # view.predict_score and exported predictor call score(..., uid=None).
    # A separate named user-aware diagnostic calls score(..., uid=uid).
    diagnosis = DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(diagnostic_loader)

    save_model_sparse_buffers_mapping_and_config_under_trial_directory()
    write_predictor_with_identical_full_training_inference_scoring()
    verify_export_and_full_catalog_parity()
    verify_exclusion_against_explicit_training_only_recounts()

# Compare baseline, last-anchor and five-anchor variants only in primary selection.
# Nine prespecified variant/milestone bundles; disclose duplicates and all scores.
# Additional diagnostic curves do not create primary selection candidates.
# Charge training, validation, diagnostics, debugging and failures to 43,200 GPU-seconds.
# Select exclusively by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10.
# Bootstrap only available host-provided per-user hits; never alter the evaluator.

originality.positive: User-excluded transition evidence, bounded fusion and explicit controls form a precise, interpretable adaptation to the diagnosed SASRec failures.
originality.negative: Sequential rules, directed item associations, popularity lift, recency aggregation, target-statistic exclusion and residual blending are established; five-anchor aggregation does not create a higher-order rule model.

future_potential.positive: Provides a controlled framework for testing when independently supported population successors complement personal causal sequence representations.
future_potential.negative: Sparse independent support, exposure confounding, training/inference statistic differences and unobserved compatibility limit coverage and practical interpretation.

code_difficulty.positive: The learned addition remains one scalar per dataset, and inference can use a precomputed sparse residual table.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact user exclusion requires sampler identities and additional sparse statistics; causal alignment, diagnostic contracts, timing and predictor parity add substantial integration work.

idea_diagnosis.description: Replace baseline SASRec's training data loss with uncorrected candidate-set cross-entropy over one observed positive and eight unique uniform eligible negatives per valid causal position. Keep architecture and inference scoring unchanged, and distinguish objective effects from competitor-count effects through matched controls.
idea_diagnosis.motivation: Electronics has the weakest supplied training margins, while qualitative feedback suggests broad associations can outrank specific matches. Multiple competitors test ranking discrimination without adding a history branch or treating uncertain ownership, compatibility or intent as dislike. Many-negative SASRec cross-entropy is established prior work; the contribution here is a controlled, budget-aware application with reproducible sampling and faithful diagnostic interfaces. Neither the diagnostics nor prior results establish improvement on the pinned validation benchmark.

Use DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']. Preserve Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl, their routing, original splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and SASREC_EPOCHS environment behavior with default 200. Run each trial on one GPU, write artifacts beneath its trial directory, and charge all training, diagnostics, debugging and failures to the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Do not access hidden tests, fetch datasets or pretrained weights, or change the host evaluator.

Keep baseline architecture, initialization, batches, optimizer, checkpoint rules and tied-embedding inference scores. Preserve the exact baseline regularization mechanism, including which parameters or embedding rows it affects and whether it is an additive penalty or optimizer weight decay. Verify baseline BCE reduction: positive-plus-negative BCE summed per valid position differs by a factor of two from averaging both labels. For the eight-negative BCE control, use softplus(-positive) plus the mean negative softplus term per valid position, preserving the one-negative data-term convention. Cross-entropy is averaged over valid positions at temperature 1. Losses still have different gradient scales; record data loss, regularization and gradient norms rather than assuming identical optimization dynamics.

Use baseline BCE, one-negative softmax and eight-negative softmax as the primary comparisons. Add eight-negative BCE as the first additional control to complete the loss-by-count comparison. One-negative softmax is exactly pairwise BPR at the same temperature and reduction. Joint multi-negative softmax is log(1 + sum(exp(negative_score - positive_score))), not averaged BPR. Eight is a predeclared candidate, not a claimed optimum; test larger counts or generalized BCE only after primary controls and only within the remaining budget. Give conditions equal tuning allocations, record completed epochs and cumulative single-GPU seconds, and compare host HR@10 against compute. Equal epochs alone do not establish compute fairness. Preserve the baseline checkpoint-selection rule and log every evaluated configuration.

For each user, sort and deduplicate catalog-valid training-history IDs. Preserve baseline history exclusions and explicitly exclude padding and the current positive. Use only allowed training information, never validation/test histories. If a shifted training target is absent from the stored history representation, insert it into the exclusion set for that position. Catalog eligibility must follow the baseline item mapping without consulting held-out interactions. Unobserved eligible items remain potentially relevant; exclusions do not eliminate false negatives.

For exact uniform sampling without replacement, convert eligible catalog IDs 1..N to zero-based indices 0..N-1. Let sorted excluded indices be h, a[j] = h[j] - j, and M = N - len(h). Draw min(K,M) distinct complement ranks using Floyd's algorithm with a dedicated seeded generator. Map each rank r to index r + searchsorted(a, r, right=True), then add one to recover item IDs. Floyd sampling uses O(K) auxiliary storage; avoid allocating randperm(M) or catalog-sized weights per position. Sort sampled ranks for stable ordering. When M<K, use all eligible items and mask absent slots. When M=0, the positive-only softmax contributes zero data loss; retain that position in the declared valid-position denominator and report its count. Assert uniqueness and exclusion invariants in sampler checks.

Gather valid prediction positions before candidate embedding lookup, avoiding B×L×K×D allocation for padded positions. Start with this simple implementation for K=8. If memory requires chunking, release candidate-scoring graphs during backward and normalize each chunk by the total valid-position count. Because chunks share backbone features, use an explicitly verified feature-gradient accumulation scheme or recomputation; repeated backward through a freed encoder graph is invalid, and summing all chunk losses before backward retains their graphs. Apply additive regularization once per optimizer step. Shared negatives would change dependence between positions and must be a separately named variant.

Use explicit random generators, stable user ordering and deterministic worker seeds. Save sampler, Python, NumPy, CPU/CUDA RNG, optimizer and scheduler states for resumed runs. Record software versions and determinism settings; seeded execution does not guarantee portability across platforms. Unit-check exact complement mapping on tiny catalogs, including consecutive exclusions and K>M. Validate empirical sampling frequencies separately from model evaluation.

The uncorrected objective deliberately optimizes sampled candidate-set competition. It needs no probability correction to define that objective, but is not an unbiased full-catalog softmax estimator. Uniform negative probabilities do not cancel against a forced positive. Any future full-softmax approximation must explicitly specify its sampling design and correction; without-replacement inclusion probability is K/M, and excluded items cannot be recovered through correction.

Inference remains the trained dot-product scorer. Preserve the predictor writer, save objective/sampler configuration with checkpoints, and verify eval-mode candidate-score parity before and after reload through generated working/predict.py for all four routes. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. view.model is the actual trained nn.Module; view.item_emb, log2feats, predict_score, user_train, meta_data and review_data retain their compatibility contracts. Restore the actual module's previous mode in finally. Preserve existing loader-negative diagnostics, distinguish optional multi-competitor diagnostics, keep unavailable metadata breakdowns empty and return null for undefined statistics.

Select exclusively using the unchanged host benchmark: 200 validation users per category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed 42, and equal-weight macro HR@10. Report category results. If authorized per-user outputs are available, derive popularity strata solely from training counts, freeze stratum boundaries before comparisons, and report denominators without changing selection. Training margins may improve through memorization or popularity shortcuts; monitor validation behavior rather than treating larger margins as generalization. The twenty training users' full-catalog recommendations remain exploratory qualitative evidence. Do not infer equipment ownership, satisfied needs, ratings, unavailable categories or simulator traits. Repeated adaptive selection on fixed validation users can overfit; limit and log configurations, and leave final held-out evaluation to the host.

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

# Catalog IDs are 1..N; 0 is padding.
def sample_complement(N, excluded_ids, K, generator):
    h = torch.tensor(sorted({int(x)-1 for x in excluded_ids
                             if 1 <= int(x) <= N}), dtype=torch.long)
    M = N - h.numel()
    k = min(K, M)
    # Floyd's algorithm: an exact uniform subset of complement ranks.
    selected = set()
    for j in range(M-k, M):
        t = int(torch.randint(j+1, (), generator=generator).item())
        selected.add(j if t in selected else t)
    ranks = torch.tensor(sorted(selected), dtype=torch.long)
    adjusted = h - torch.arange(h.numel())
    ids = ranks + torch.searchsorted(adjusted, ranks, right=True) + 1

    result[:k] = ids
    return result


def multi_negative_loss(features, positive, negatives, item_emb):
    # features [B,L,D], positive [B,L], negatives [B,L,K].
    valid = positive.ne(0)
    f = features[valid]
    p = positive[valid]
    n = negatives[valid]
    if p.numel() == 0:
        return features.sum() * 0.0
    candidates = torch.cat([p[:, None], n], dim=1)
    # Gather valid positions before lookup; K=8 normally needs no chunking.
    logits = torch.einsum('vd,vkd->vk', f, item_emb(candidates))
    logits = logits.masked_fill(candidates.eq(0), float('-inf'))
    labels = torch.zeros(p.numel(), dtype=torch.long, device=f.device)
    return F.cross_entropy(logits, labels, reduction='sum') / p.numel()

    source = sum_counts_by_source(counts)
    target = sum_counts_by_target(counts)
    total = sum(counts.values())
    user_outdegree, user_indegree = sparse_user_edge_degrees(edges_by_user)

    def edge_residual(source_ids, candidates, uid=None):
        # Explicit broadcasting must preserve batch, position and candidate axes.
        c = sparse_edge_lookup(counts, source_ids, candidates, default=0)
        C = lookup(source, source_ids, default=0)
        T = lookup(target, candidates, default=0)
        M = total
        if uid is not None:
            # uid is explicit and correctly broadcast for each training example.
            c = c - user_edge_membership(edges_by_user, uid, source_ids, candidates)
            C = C - lookup(user_outdegree, uid, source_ids, default=0)
            T = T - lookup(user_indegree, uid, candidates, default=0)
            M = M - user_edge_count(edges_by_user, uid)
        p0 = (T + 1.0) / (M + num_real_items)
        conditional = (c + 20.0 * p0) / (C + 20.0)
        lift = clip(log(conditional / p0), 0.0, 2.0)
        value = C / (C + 10.0) * c / (c + 3.0) * lift
        return where((c > 0) & (source_ids != 0) & (candidates != 0), value, 0.0)

    model = BaselineSASRecWithSparseResidual(training_only_statistics)
    model.theta = Parameter(logit(0.01 / 2.0))

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

# Catalog IDs are 1..N; 0 is padding.
def sample_complement(N, excluded_ids, K, generator):
    h = torch.tensor(sorted({int(x)-1 for x in excluded_ids
                             if 1 <= int(x) <= N}), dtype=torch.long)
    M = N - h.numel()
    k = min(K, M)
    # Floyd's algorithm: an exact uniform subset of complement ranks.
    selected = set()
    for j in range(M-k, M):
        t = int(torch.randint(j+1, (), generator=generator).item())
        selected.add(j if t in selected else t)
    ranks = torch.tensor(sorted(selected), dtype=torch.long)
    adjusted = h - torch.arange(h.numel())
    ids = ranks + torch.searchsorted(adjusted, ranks, right=True) + 1
    result = torch.zeros(K, dtype=torch.long)
    result[:k] = ids
    return result


def multi_negative_loss(features, positive, negatives, item_emb):
    # features [B,L,D], positive [B,L], negatives [B,L,K].
    valid = positive.ne(0)
    f = features[valid]
    p = positive[valid]
    n = negatives[valid]
    if p.numel() == 0:
        return features.sum() * 0.0
    candidates = torch.cat([p[:, None], n], dim=1)
    # Gather valid positions before lookup; K=8 normally needs no chunking.
    logits = torch.einsum('vd,vkd->vk', f, item_emb(candidates))
    logits = logits.masked_fill(candidates.eq(0), float('-inf'))
    labels = torch.zeros(p.numel(), dtype=torch.long, device=f.device)

Three starting-point insights guide this proposal. First, SASRec already models causal sequence dependencies; a small residual permits an interpretable intervention.             return found.float()
        return torch.where(found, values[safe], 0.0)

    def log2feats(self, seq: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        hidden = self._backbone_feats(seq)
        if self.transition_anchors == 0:
            return hidden
        # Compact each prefix by interaction count, preserving repeated items.
        ranks = (seq != 0).long().cumsum(dim=1)
        compact = torch.zeros(
            (seq.shape[0], seq.shape[1] + 1), dtype=torch.long, device=seq.device
        )
        compact.scatter_add_(1, ranks, seq)
        anchors = []
        for age in range(self.transition_anchors):
            index = (ranks - age).clamp_min(0)
            anchors.append(compact.gather(1, index))
        anchors = torch.stack(anchors, dim=-1)
        packed = anchors.double()
        if not torch.equal(packed.long(), anchors):
            raise RuntimeError("Anchor IDs failed exact float64 packing")
        return torch.cat((hidden.double(), packed), dim=-1)

    def _user_rows(self, user_ids):
        if self.training_users.numel() == 0:
            raise ValueError("User-excluded scoring requires training identities")
        rows = torch.searchsorted(self.training_users, user_ids.contiguous())
        safe = rows.clamp_max(self.training_users.numel() - 1)
        if not bool(
            (
                (rows < self.training_users.numel())
                & (self.training_users[safe] == user_ids)
            ).all()
        ):
            raise ValueError("Unknown training user identity")
        return rows

    def _edge_lift(self, sources, items, user_rows=None):
        sources, items = torch.broadcast_tensors(sources, items)
        stride = self.itemnum + 1
        query = sources * stride + items
        if user_rows is None:
            # Counts are immutable between checkpoint loads. Build once rather
            # than recomputing probabilities for every catalog candidate chunk.
            if self._inference_lift is None:
                with torch.no_grad():
                    source_ids = self.edge_keys // stride
                    target_ids = self.edge_keys % stride
                    c_full = self.edge_counts
                    C_full = self.source_mass[source_ids]
                    p0_full = (self.target_mass[target_ids] + 1.0) / (
                        self.total_mass + self.itemnum
                    )
                    conditional_full = (c_full + 20.0 * p0_full) / (C_full + 20.0)
                    self._inference_lift = (
                        C_full
                        / (C_full + 10.0)
                        * c_full
                        / (c_full + 3.0)
                        * torch.log(conditional_full / p0_full).clamp(0.0, 2.0)
                    )
            value = self._lookup(self.edge_keys, query, self._inference_lift)
            return torch.where((sources != 0) & (items != 0), value, 0.0)
        c = self._lookup(self.edge_keys, query, self.edge_counts)
        C = self.source_mass[sources]
        T = self.target_mass[items]
        M = self.total_mass
        if user_rows is not None:
            user_rows = user_rows.expand_as(items)
            if self.edge_keys.numel():
                edge_index = torch.searchsorted(self.edge_keys, query.contiguous())
                safe = edge_index.clamp_max(self.edge_keys.numel() - 1)
                observed = (edge_index < self.edge_keys.numel()) & (
                    self.edge_keys[safe] == query
                )
                membership_key = user_rows * self.edge_keys.numel() + safe
                c = c - observed.float() * self._lookup(
                    self.user_edge_keys, membership_key
                )
            C = C - self._lookup(
                self.user_source_keys,
                user_rows * stride + sources,
                self.user_source_values,
            )
            T = T - self._lookup(
                self.user_target_keys,
                user_rows * stride + items,
                self.user_target_values,
            )
            M = M - self.user_mass[user_rows]
        p0 = (T + 1.0) / (M + self.itemnum)
        conditional = (c + 20.0 * p0) / (C + 20.0)
        lift = torch.log(conditional / p0).clamp(0.0, 2.0)
        value = C / (C + 10.0) * c / (c + 3.0) * lift
        return torch.where((c > 0) & (sources != 0) & (items != 0), value, 0.0)

    def _score(self, features, items, user_ids=None, fixed_amplitude=None):
        items = torch.as_tensor(items, dtype=torch.long, device=features.device)
        if features.ndim == 2 and items.ndim == 1:
            items = items.unsqueeze(0).expand(features.shape[0], -1)
        hidden = features[..., : self.hidden_units].to(self.item_emb.weight.dtype)
        extra_axes = items.ndim - (hidden.ndim - 1)
        if extra_axes < 0:
            raise ValueError("Candidates must preserve batch and position axes")
        # Reject accidental cross-user/position broadcasting. Shared final-state
        # candidate vectors were explicitly expanded above.
        feature_shape = tuple(hidden.shape[:-1])
        if tuple(items.shape[: len(feature_shape)]) != feature_shape:
            raise ValueError("Candidate batch and position axes must match features")
        aligned = hidden
        for _ in range(extra_axes):
            aligned = aligned.unsqueeze(-2)
        base = (aligned * self.item_emb(items)).sum(dim=-1)
        if self.transition_anchors == 0:
            return base
        user_rows = None
        if user_ids is not None:
            user_ids = torch.as_tensor(
                user_ids, dtype=torch.long, device=features.device
            )
            if user_ids.shape != (features.shape[0],):
                raise ValueError(
                    "Exactly one explicit user ID is required per sequence"
                )
            user_rows = self._user_rows(user_ids)
            user_rows = user_rows.reshape((-1,) + (1,) * (items.ndim - 1))
        anchors = features[..., self.hidden_units :].long()
        numerator = torch.zeros_like(base)
        denominator = torch.zeros_like(hidden[..., 0])
        for age in range(self.transition_anchors):
            source = anchors[..., age]
            weight = (2.0 ** (-age / 2.0)) * (source != 0).to(base.dtype)
            denominator = denominator + weight
            for _ in range(extra_axes):
                source = source.unsqueeze(-1)
                weight = weight.unsqueeze(-1)
            numerator = numerator + weight * self._edge_lift(source, items, user_rows)
        for _ in range(extra_axes):
            denominator = denominator.unsqueeze(-1)
        residual = numerator / denominator.clamp_min(1e-8)
        amplitude = 2.0 * torch.sigmoid(self.theta)
        if fixed_amplitude is not None:
            if not 0.0 <= float(fixed_amplitude) <= 2.0:
                raise ValueError("Diagnostic amplitude must lie in [0, 2]")
            amplitude = float(fixed_amplitude)
        return base + amplitude * residual

    def predict_score(self, features, items):
        # Public diagnostics and inference deliberately use full training counts.
        return self._score(features, items)

    def training_score(self, features, items, user_ids):
        return self._score(features, items, user_ids=user_ids)

    def forward(
        self,
        seq: torch.Tensor,
        pos: torch.Tensor | None = None,
        neg: torch.Tensor | None = None,
        user_ids=None,
    ):
        features = self.log2feats(seq)
        if pos is None or neg is None:
            return features
        if self.training and self.transition_anchors and user_ids is None:
            raise ValueError("Training residuals require explicit user identities")
        if pos.shape != seq.shape or neg.shape != seq.shape:
            raise ValueError("Training targets must match the B x L sequence shape")
        # Resolve user rows and construct anchor weights once for both labels.
        logits = self._score(
            features, torch.stack((pos, neg), dim=-1), user_ids=user_ids
        )
        return logits[..., 0], logits[..., 1]

    def predict(self, seq: torch.Tensor, candidates: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        features = self.log2feats(seq)
        positions = torch.arange(seq.shape[1], device=seq.device).expand_as(seq)
        last = positions.masked_fill(seq == 0, -1).amax(dim=1).clamp_min(0)
        final = features[torch.arange(seq.shape[0], device=seq.device), last]
        return self.predict_score(final, candidates)

    ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END


# ── Validation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def evaluate_val(
    model: SASRec,
    user_train: dict,
    user_valid: dict,
    itemnum: int,
    device: torch.device,
    maxlen: int = 128,
    num_users: int = 200,
) -> dict[str, float]:
    ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Keep validation deterministic without perturbing training sampling
    rng = random.Random(42)
    val_users = [u for u in user_valid if u in user_train]
    if len(val_users) > num_users:
        val_users = rng.sample(val_users, num_users)
    ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END

    HR10 = HR20 = NDCG10 = NDCG20 = 0.0
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for u in val_users:
            pos_items = user_valid[u]
            if not pos_items:
                continue
            target = pos_items[0]

            hist = user_train[u][-maxlen:]
            seq_arr = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int32)
            for i, item in enumerate(reversed(hist)):
                seq_arr[maxlen - 1 - i] = item

            seq_t = torch.tensor(seq_arr, dtype=torch.long, device=device).unsqueeze(0)
            neg_pool: set[int] = set()
            interacted = set(user_train[u]) | set(pos_items)
            while len(neg_pool) < 99:
                ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Use the isolated validation candidate RNG
                ni = rng.randint(1, itemnum)
                ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END
                if ni not in interacted:
                    neg_pool.add(ni)
            candidates = [target] + list(neg_pool)

            cand_t = torch.tensor([candidates], dtype=torch.long, device=device)
            scores = model.predict(seq_t, cand_t)[0].cpu().numpy().tolist()
            rank = sorted(range(len(candidates)), key=lambda i: -scores[i]).index(0)

            HR10 += 1.0 if rank < 10 else 0.0
            HR20 += 1.0 if rank < 20 else 0.0
            NDCG10 += (1.0 / math.log2(rank + 2)) if rank < 10 else 0.0
            NDCG20 += (1.0 / math.log2(rank + 2)) if rank < 20 else 0.0

    n = max(len(val_users), 1)
    model.train()
    return {
        "HR@10": HR10 / n,
        "HR@20": HR20 / n,
        "NDCG@10": NDCG10 / n,
        "NDCG@20": NDCG20 / n,
    }

            pos_labels = torch.ones(pos_logits[indices].shape, device=device)

            loss = bce_criterion(pos_logits[indices], pos_labels)
            loss = loss + bce_criterion(neg_logits[indices], neg_labels)

            optimizer.zero_grad()

            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 5.0)
            optimizer.step()
            total_loss += loss.item()

            ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Report paired full-count and excluded-count training diagnostics
